decisions.title: API Gateway: Kong selected over AWS API Gateway
decisions.rationale: Vendor independence, richer plugin ecosystem, lower long-term lock-in risk. AWS API Gateway would couple us to AWS IAM auth model incompatible with multi-cloud partner requirements.

decisions.title: Auth: JWT RS256 with 1-hour access tokens and 30-day refresh
decisions.rationale: RS256 allows public-key verification by partners without sharing secrets. Short-lived tokens limit breach window. 30-day refresh balances UX against revocation latency.

decisions.title: Rate limiting: Redis-backed sliding window per partner
decisions.rationale: Sliding window more accurate than fixed window for burst detection. Per-partner quotas isolate noisy neighbors. Redis chosen for low latency.

decisions.title: Observability: Prometheus + Grafana + Jaeger
decisions.rationale: Standard open-source stack. Jaeger for distributed tracing across gateway → auth → partner callbacks. Avoids vendor lock-in on observability.

decisions.title: Redis circuit-breaker: Bob to draft design by 2026-04-30
decisions.rationale: Arch review surfaced Redis SPOF. Design needed before Redis goes to staging.

decisions.title: Token scope model: two tiers (partner:read, partner:write)
decisions.rationale: Simplest model that satisfies Partner A and Partner B requirements. Read-only partners default to read scope; write requires explicit grant at onboarding. Avoids per-endpoint ACL complexity.

decisions.title: Redis → AWS ElastiCache migration for at-rest encryption
decisions.rationale: ElastiCache supports KMS encryption natively. Avoids Redis Enterprise licensing cost (~$18k/yr). Required for HIPAA compliance (PHI-adjacent rate limiting data).

decisions.title: Partner B deferred to Phase 2 if no response by May 19
decisions.rationale: Team cannot hold HIPAA scope open indefinitely. May 19 gives two weeks post-questionnaire deadline. Deferral allows M2 to proceed without Partner B blocking auth service staging.
